definition.simple: A technique used to separate those mixtures where the different parts dissolve in the same liquid but travel at different speeds.
definition.academic: A laboratory technique for the separation of a mixture into its components, in which the mixture is passed through a stationary phase (like paper) by a mobile phase (like a solvent).

examples: Separating the different colored dyes found in black ink.

common_misconceptions: Chromatography only separates colors. (False: It was originally used for colors (chroma = color), but today it is used to separate many invisible chemicals too!).
ai_context.tutor_hint: The component that is more soluble in water rises faster on the filter paper!
